title: Missing Value Detection MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Count the missing values that isnull() will find in a column of a small DataFrame, check your answer, and reveal the hidden missing values that pandas does not detect.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to apply isnull() and isnull().sum() to count the missing values in a DataFrame and identify hidden missing values that isnull() does not detect.
prerequisites: Rows, columns, and cells of a DataFrame
NaN as the pandas marker for a missing value

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice with immediate feedback: predict a count, check it, then reveal the mask
keyQuestions: Why does isnull() return False for an empty string?
How would you turn -999 into a value that isnull() can find?
In scenario 5, would you drop the rows with missing values? What would be left?
commonMisconceptions: isnull() finds everything that is missing (it finds only NaN and None, not empty strings or placeholder codes).
A blank-looking cell is always NaN (it may hold an empty string, which pandas treats as a value).
A number such as -999 must be real data (legacy systems often use it to mean no value).
assessmentOpportunities: Shown a printed DataFrame that contains NaN, None, an empty string, and -999, students state the output of df.isnull().sum() for each column, give the total and the percentage missing, and name the cells that are missing but not counted.
